title: Chest pain in an older adult
setting: Community clinic consultation room, late afternoon
description: A 72-year-old man presents with heavy central chest pain that started while he was resting.

speaker.name: Johannes van der Merwe
speaker.language: English; he is more comfortable speaking Afrikaans
speaker.style: Stoic and private. He tends to minimise his pain and may say he is fine even when he is clearly sweating and uncomfortable. He is worried about troubling his wife.

patient.name: Johannes van der Merwe
patient.living_situation: Lives with his wife on a smallholding outside town

presenting_complaint: Heavy central chest pain at rest, radiating to the left arm and jaw, with sweating, nausea, and shortness of breath.
opening_line: Sister, my chest feels heavy, like something is pressing on it. It started while I was sitting, and now my arm and jaw are sore. I also feel sweaty and a little sick.
personality: Stoic, polite, and reluctant to complain. He downplays symptoms and may need gentle direct questions. He is anxious about his wife being left alone.

history.onset: About 45 minutes ago while he was sitting and watching television. It has not eased with rest.
history.character: Heavy, crushing central chest pain, severity 9 out of 10. He says it feels like a weight on his chest.
history.radiation: The pain spreads to the left arm and jaw.
history.previous_episode: He had a similar but milder episode last week that lasted a few minutes and went away. He did not seek care.
history.past_medical_history: High blood pressure for about fifteen years. Type 2 diabetes for ten years. High cholesterol.
history.medications: Amlodipine 10 mg daily, metformin 1 g twice daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg daily. He does not take aspirin.
history.social_history: Ex-smoker with a 20 pack-year history, quit ten years ago. Occasional brandy. Retired farmer. Lives with his wife.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Suspected acute coronary syndrome, possibly myocardial infarction
red_flags: central crushing chest pain lasting more than twenty minutes at rest
radiation to the left arm and jaw
older age with diabetes and hypertension
expected_actions: call emergency services or activate the local emergency response immediately
keep the patient seated or lying comfortably and do not send him home
check observations, oxygen saturation, and blood glucose
obtain a twelve-lead ECG within ten minutes if available
give aspirin 300 mg chewed if there is no contraindication and local protocol allows
give oxygen only if hypoxic according to local protocol
consider glyceryl trinitrate if protocol allows and there are no contraindications
reassure the patient, explain the plan in plain language, and arrange urgent transfer

learning_objectives: Recognise the red flags of a time-critical cardiac emergency
Communicate urgency and reassurance to a stoic older patient
